title: Beautiful Towers II
summary: Given an array maxHeights of n integers, construct n towers at coordinates 0 to n-1.
statement: Given an array maxHeights of n integers, construct n towers at coordinates 0 to n-1. Each tower's height must not exceed the corresponding maxHeights value. A beautiful configuration requires the heights to form a mountain, where the heights strictly increase to a peak and then strictly decrease. The task is to find the maximum sum of the tower heights that meets these criteria.
constraints: Choose positive tower heights no greater than max_heights.
Heights must be nondecreasing up to one peak and nonincreasing afterward; maximize their sum.
hints: For each peak, each side is forced down only when a cap becomes smaller.
Use monotonic stacks to compute the maximum capped prefix and suffix sums for every peak.
Combine left[i]+right[i]-peak height and take the maximum.
The nearest lower cap controls a whole span, so stack jumps reuse the already optimal sum before that span.
editorial: The nearest lower cap controls a whole span, so stack jumps reuse the already optimal sum before that span.

tests.explanation: Using heights 5,3,3,1,1 with the first position as peak gives the maximum sum thirteen.
The best capped mountain has sum twenty-two.
